My armor? Special issue. By the Duke's request. It's part of his guards' uniform.

A fairly lightweight, flexible armor that offers some of the highest protection available, and is made from special adamantium ore found on rare deposits on the mainland. Most of the adamantium armor here on the mainland is shipped through Ebonheart.
Most of the dunmer armors can't compare to good nordic mail, but adamantium armor has all the feel of a good steel. It's rather ornamental for my tastes, although you can't argue with results.

All my armor is specialty made. I am selling a mostly complete set, too. Helms have been in short supply, unfortunately. I don't know if anyone has been able to get a hand on one. Adamantium armor is costly to make, as adamantium mines are less common than ebony or glass deposits.

One of the more ornate dunmer armors, adamantium armor offers higher protection than orcish, but less protection than ebony. It is rather rare and expensive to produce, but the mainland offers some relatively untapped deposits of the elusive adamantium ore that have recently been made available, allowing for a more recent influx of product.
Aradraen recently opened up a fletching shop here in the lower waistworks. She specializes in enchanted arrows, bolts, and darts.

I've heard rumor in Dagon Fel that there is a wondrous helm to be found in the ruins of Onnissiralis. It is a large Daedric shrine far to the north of Vvardenfell, west of a place called Vas. It's been suggested I seek out the brothers Norvayne, who have left recently to investigate the ruins.

I have met the Norvayne brothers, Dalin and Daris. They seem undecided on how they wish to proceed with the exploration of the ruin. Dalin feels that the more people involved, the better the chances of survival. Daris believes that it is a matter of family honor that they explore it alone.
The brothers have decided to work out their differences in their own way: a fistfight. Whoever is left standing will be the one to decide how they will proceed.
Dalin has bested his brother in hand-to-hand combat.
The brothers will now follow me into the ruins, as Dalin has won the "argument" with his brother.
Daris has bested his brother in hand-to-hand combat.

Dalin Norvayne has been killed.
Daris Norvayne has been killed.

Excellent! My brother Daris and I were just discussing the same thing. Years ago, our father perished in these ruins, may he rest well. We wish to clear the place of the evil that resides inside. I believe that the more who will help us, the better. My brother believes that it is a matter of family honor, and we must do it ourselves.

The brothers Norvayne left here recently to investigate the ruins of Onnissiralis to recover a family heirloom. I don't know exactly where it is, but I'd overheard them heading out west past Vas. Here, I'll mark Vas on your map. It may be worth seeing if they need help. They're good folks, if a bit argumentative.

I know your stance on this, Dalin! My brother speaks out of turn. It seems there is only one way for us to settle this. It is a time-honored Norvayne family tradition. Do not interfere, stranger. When our decision is made, we will let you know.

Enough, Daris! Please excuse my brother. It seems there is only one way for us to settle this. It is a time-honored Norvayne family tradition. Please, do not interfere. When our decision is made, we will let you know.
Good luck in your adventures, friend.

You have found what you seek. You should continue on your own for now. I will stay in this place, and give my brother a burial he would be proud of. I wish my brother were able to see this, but I know his and my father's spirit will be watching over me.

You have found what you seek, friend. You should continue on your own for now. My brother and I will stay in this place for now. I was wrong to doubt you, and I acknowledge that. Best of luck to you, and thank you for helping us avenge our father.
You were not to interfere! Now you face us both!

Because you were respectful, you're welcome to our father's old key. We are only interested in vengeance, but you may find use for it. Good luck to you.

My brother bested me, though it could have gone either way. As he has won the argument, we will follow you into the ruins. Since we are working together, you should take this key. It belonged to our father. As we are only interested in vengeance, you're welcome to take whatever you find with it. Now, let us go.
Greetings, %PCRace. Please leave us alone. Our intent to explore these ruins is a family matter, and does not concern you.

You have found what you seek. I will miss my brother, and will stay here to ensure I can properly bury him. You should continue on your own for now. Please, remember the Norvayne name as you continue your adventures.

You see, I was able to divine the recipe to craft a special token.. Using what I believe is a forgotten Dwemer technique, I've been able to create these special Fast Travel Tokens. With these, you'd be able to instantly travel to many previous locations that you've already been to by touching a signpost. I might be willing to part with some, for a cost...

As you probably guessed, I'm with the Mage's Guild. I'm honestly pretty bored, none of these people seem to have any real magical ability to speak of nor do they have access to any interesting knowledge. I was assigned here, to this pit, and while I was trying to slip away to a quiet place I came across a gem that was unlike anything I've ever seen before. After studying this gem for some time I was able to divine some incredible knowledge from it...

You again?! I'm not sure why you're up here or if I should be worried that you are.. but I suppose you'd have attacked me already if you were going to. Maybe you can be useful, maybe we can come to an agreement?

While exploring Nchuleftingth I found an Altmer, Kelkemmelian Adorin. He seemed to be avoiding the other Mage's Guild members and complained about the Guild in general. He made a cryptic reference to Fast Travel Tokens and seemed to offer to sell or trade for them.

Kelkemmelian Adorin says he has enchanted "Fast Travel Tokens" that would allow me to quickly travel to almost any location I've been to previously by simply touching any signpost. He's charging either one Dwemer coin or 5000 gold for each.. could be worth it. I should find him in Nchuleftingth if I need any.
I've used one of the Fast Travel Tokens I got from Kelkemmelian Adorin. They do work as intended and should allow me to move about much more quickly.

Kwama colonies, also known as eggmines, are home to the large creatures known as kwama. They are pock-marked with tunnels carved out by the foragers and workers. The former spray rock with acid to soften it, while the latter use their hard beaks to dig through the softened material. Egg miners must often use picks to widen tunnels too narrow to pass through in order to gather the precious kwama eggs.

Kwama eggs are one of the most popular sources of protein in Morrowind. They stay fresh for a long time and their soft shells make them relatively easy to transport, which has made them popular throughout the Empire. Mind yourself around the eggs though, outlander. The mature ones will splash you with acid if you get too close. Look for the eggs that throb slightly. If you hear a scream: run.

Kwama eggs are one of the most popular sources of protein in Morrowind. They stay fresh for a long time and their soft shells make them relatively easy to transport which has spread their popularity throughout the empire. Mind yourself around the eggs though, %PCRace. The mature ones will splash you with acid if you get too close. Look for the eggs that throb slightly. If you hear a scream: run.

The kwama forager scouts the surface of the land and natural underground passages, searching for suitable locations for new colonies, and hunting for prey. Foragers are aggressive but not very dangerous. When they return, they are often severely engorged with food for the colony. They will then be suspended in a place where they can provide nourishment to other kwama. I'd recommend avoiding any such foragers you see, lest you stimulate them to regurgitate their food onto yourself.

The kwama queen is the huge, bloated kwama that produces the colony's eggs and their meaty, blood-filled nests. The queens are too large and fat to move, and all their needs are attended by worker kwama.

I’m a clerk. As such, I’m responsible for keeping accurate records of all activities within my organization. I possess the knowledge to understand a variety of documents, perform basic mathematical calculations, and discuss the laws and regulations governing my organization.

I am a sailor. I'm most at home on a ship on the sea. I know how to tie a good strong knot and which gods to pray to when it storms. I'm a brawler by nature and I've hardened my knuckles fighting in so many different ports I've lost count. If the going gets really tough, I'm no stranger to the cutlass. Most sailors in Morrowind serve in the Imperial Navy or aboard merchant vessels. Some daring rascals turn to piracy.

I am a miner. Usually, here on Vvardenfell, being a miner means you're an eggminer. Scrib jerky, scrib jelly, kwama eggs, and kwama cuttle are the basis of our Vvardenfell economy, and they all come from kwama. Yes, there are more valuable resources we take from mines -- raw ebony, raw glass, dreugh wax, daedra skin, daedra heart, diamond, ash salts, and so forth -- and that's good work, too. But it's the eggminers that feed Morrowind, and bring cash from all over the Empire.
As a grocer, I stock quality produce, dry goods, and other food items. I manage my own inventory so I can make sure my shelves are full and my customers satisfied.

I’m the foreman in charge here. I organize the workers to complete the project. I have the supervisory and technical skills required to ensure that the work is done efficiently and that resources are managed wisely. My employer doesn’t want his investment wasted.

I am a weaver. I make my living by creating intricate fabrics and garments. I use a loom to create cloth from natural fibers such as wool, cotton, or silk. My skill lies in my knowledge of fibers and patterns and my ability to create desirable products with them, as well as in my long years of practice at the loom.

As a surgeon, I specialize in diagnosing and treating medical conditions without the aid of magic. I can identify ailments quickly and then perform a variety of surgical procedures as required. I am knowledgeable in the latest treatments and have a good understanding of anatomy.

I’m a butcher. I am responsible for the slaughter and preparation of animals into meat that's fit for the kitchens of my customers. I use my knowledge of animal anatomy to ensure nothing goes to waste.

I am an author, which means I use the written word to evoke emotion and shape opinion - or just tell a great story. Ideally, my patron or my adoring public pay me for those works. I have my preferred genres, but literature comes in many formats and I dabble in the others from time to time.

I am a sculptor. I create works of art out of stone, metal, and other materials. I use my eye for detail to transform a block of material into something remarkable. My knowledge of sculpting techniques and raw materials allows me to bring life to my creations.

I’m a painter. I use a variety of mediums to capture my creative vision on canvas, be it something as simple as a summer day, or something as short-lived as a noblewoman’s youth. From landscapes to portraits, I take delight in mixing colors and seeking out the perfect composition.
I have no trade. Down on my luck, you see. Spare a coin?

The pomegranate is a succulent shrub that produces fruit with a sweet and tart flavored juice that is popularly fermented into wine. Pomegranates primarily grow in the Molag Amur region but have grown scarce due to the spread of the Blight. The few surviving fruit-bearing plants have developed a resistance to blight disease.

The scrib is a late larval form of the kwama. Towards the end of their life-cycle, scrib will encase themselves in a cocoon where they transform into either the male forager or female worker. The sharp tips of their legs secrete a mild paralyzing agent which they use to escape predators. Crushed scribs produce a nutritious but sour-tasting gelatin that goes well with wickwheat bread.

The scrib is a late larval form of the kwama. Towards the end of their life-cycle, scrib will encase themselves in a cocoon where they transform into either the male forager or female worker. Yes, it’s my speciality. Adamantium is a rare and expensive material. By mixing it up with netch leather, you can make equipment that works just as well -  if not better - than a full set of adamantium armour, and you don’t have to spend a fortune to protect yourself!
Walk with reverence in the presence of the dead. Show them respect, and you will be shown respect in kind.

There are some outlanders who confuse our sacred magic with necromancy. To one unfamiliar with our ways, this is an understandable mistake, but be aware that many faithful Dunmer may take offense to such a misunderstanding.

I have heard disquieting rumors of outlanders ransacking ancestral tombs in search of treasure. They think that just because a place is empty they have the right to defile it. Not only do they steal and disturb the dead, but they violate their very remains as well. I can hardly fathom such disgraceful actions, but rest assured graverobbers meet swift and severe punishment at the hands of the tomb guardians.

Yes, this is the legendary Lord's Mail, %PCRank. As reward, you are welcome in our Order here. Take this suit of armor reserved for the Order of Ebonheart. I have another task for you. I want you to find Chrysamere.
Greetings traveller. I'm Cythus, warrior and smith. I specialize in the craftmanship of netch adamantium armor. Interested?
Greetings, pilgrim! I, Shulki Ashunbabi, have the finest wares in Gnisis!

I am %Name, an Ancestral Mage of the Temple. We are taught the ancestral arts in the sacred city of Necrom, and then sent to holy sites within Morrowind to perform our magics in service of the Tribunal.
I'm a skilled warrior and smith, but I prefer to earn a living by selling the armours I make rather than working as a mercenary.

My duties are primarily ancestral summoning and constructing security to protect against tomb raiders. I am well versed in the arts of crafting undead servants such as bonewalkers, bonelords, and skeletons, as well as binding guardian spirits.
As an Ancestral Mage, my services would regrettably be of no use to an outlander such as yourself.
Nice to see you.
Greetings to you.
A pleasure to meet you.
It's so good to see you.
This is an honor.
Your actions precede you, outlander.
Greetings outlander, I think I've heard of you before.
Greetings, outlander.
Welcome friend.
To what do I owe the honor?
For the glory of Tiber Septim, it is an honor to be in its service. Although clearly this is something that *you* do not understand.
For the glory of Tiber Septim, it is an honor to be in its service.
Hail to the Knight of the Imperial Dragon!
%PCRank.
It's up on the hill, on the east side of town. Careful in there, the kwama queen has been blighted.
It's up on the hill, on the east side of town. Because the kwama queen has been blighted we are only granting access to miners at this time.

I have spoken to Molag Bal through his statue in the shrine at Bal Ur. He tells me that he does not have the cure for my vampirism, but he will get it for me if I do him a favor. His daughter, Molag Grunda, has been consorting with a Frost Atronach named Nomeg Gwai. If I can kill the two of them, returning their souls to a realm where Molag Bal may punish them, Molag Bal will give me the cure. They live now in the cave Dubdilla, west of Mount Assarnibibi.
Scholar on the Mount

I met a merchant by the name of Salk Zama-Nanu in Molag Mar whose personal copy of a Guide to Vvardenfell was taken by an overzealous Temple scholar in her quest to reach Mount Assarnibibi. He said she mentioned pomegranates and Molag Bal before she took off with his scroll. He kindly asked me to search for it on the summit of the mountain and return it to him in the Suran Tradehouse where he expects to be soon hereafter.
I lied about properly searching Mount Assarnibibi to Salk Zama-Nanu. He seemed disappointed.
I found a satchel containing a copy of a Guide to Vvardenfell signed by one Salk Zama-Nanu. Perhaps someone in Molag Mar would recognize the name.

I found a satchel containing Salk Zama-Nanu's scroll on Mount Assarnibibi. There's no trace of the scholar other than a half-eaten pomegranate. I can only assume that she met her end on this venture. I should return the guide scroll to its owner in the Suran Tradehouse.
Salk Zama-Nanu was sad to hear about the scholar's fate but very grateful to have his copy of a Guide to Vvardenfell returned.
Oh yes, I know Salk Zama-Nanu. He's a Velothi food merchant who travels on my caravan regularly. In fact I just transported him and his goods to Suran.
A merchant, I believe. Dilami Androm the caravaner might know him.
Yes, I know Salk Zama-Nanu. He's a food merchant. He was just here recently. Perhaps Dilami Androm, the caravaner, might have an idea of where he was headed next.
A merchant did arrive on the last caravan from Molag Mar. The tradehouse was his most likely destination.
He's at the bar.
He's standing right over there.

Pomegranate shrubs grow in Molag Amur. Well, they did before the blight. Most died off when the red wind blew across these lands. Some still survive in sheltered areas but harvesting from them is a dangerous business. When I was still in the tribe, we would brew a tea from the fruit to rejuvenate our spirits. I'm afraid such delicacies are beyond my reach now.

Yes. You see, most traders will still only pay what a pomegranate was worth ten years ago. Supply, demand, and all that, you know. That fruit is worth more now and I'd be willing to pay what it's worth -- less my profit margin, naturally -- for any you bring my way. Unlike those pilgrims, I have less qualms about accepting forbidden fruit. You don't need to sign a contract or anything like that, just bring any intact pomegranates you find my way and I'll pay you handsomely.

You say that you found pomegranates on Mount Assarnibibi? Yes, pilgrims do occasionally return with a pomegranate or two. But most won't touch them due to the site's history with the daedra, Molag Bal. Since you bring it up, I have a proposition for you.
Let's see here, one... [Salk counts the pomegranates and pays you accordingly].
You have some pomegranates to sell? Let me see.
Remember. If you bring me any pomegranates, I'll pay higher than anyone else on Vvardenfell!
I will be on the next caravan bound for Suran. Likely I will be gone by the time you return. Look for me in the tradehouse there. May Azura watch over you.

She kept talking about Mount Assarnibibi, a holy mountain. Something about pomegranates and Molag Bal. I admit when she uttered that depraved name, I was indisposed to aid her. But if you follow the ash pavement east from the strider port here in Molag Mar, you'll want to take the second path on your left which splits off north. That will take you to the summit. Here, I will mark it on your map. It isn't far, but the wastes are not a friendly place. I know. Oh, one last thing...

I'm not even a guide! Just a humble Velothi food merchant. That's why I keep meticulous notes on that scroll. Even when I roamed with the Ashlanders, I never strayed far from camp. I'm no hunter. I just sell food, I don't catch it. I need that scroll -- it represents years of notekeeping while on the road. And it would do my soul good to know if that poor scholar survived her foolish trek into the wastes. I'd pay half in advance, but I'm afraid I won't have any spare coin until I sell this stock in Suran.

Thank you for listening. A few days back, a Temple scholar asked me to guide her to Mount Assarnibibi. She was clearly excited about something and ultimately took off without settling on terms for the arrangement or offering any payment at all. I worry that she left with the impression that I was following behind to bring supplies for her expedition. To make matters worse, she snatched my copy of a guide to Vvardenfell while I was talking to Dilami about the shipment I was waiting on.
I understand.

That is tragic to hear you say, outlander. On both counts. May she find peace in the spirit world. And it seems that I will have to be content with my memory of Vvardenfell for now without my notes. I will hold to my end of the bargain and pay you for your trouble regardless.
I wonder then that you came here to Suran first. I thought you were going to seek the scroll for me.
It is a pleasure to see you, %PCName. I expect I will be in Suran for some time.
I have business to attend to, outlander. You'll understand that I have no more time for talk.

Thank you, muthsera. Thank you. This scroll represents years of my life. But it is a sad thing to imagine what became of that foolish scholar. You and I both know all too well the dangers the wilderness of Vvardenfell poses to the untrained. Regardless, I am grateful; and as promised, I have your payment thanks to my successful profits here in Suran. I would also like you to have this kwama egg. Prepared in a way considered a delicacy here in Morrowind. Please, enjoy. And may you find all that you seek.
Oh, %PCName, it makes me happy to see you alive and well. Were you able to find the scholar and recover my guide to Vvardenfell scroll?

That is a pity. A foolish scholar took the guide from me before venturing to Mount Assarnibibi on her own. Jabbering about pomegranates and Molag Bal. I had hoped that she was alive, but I fear that is not the case. Please accept this payment for finding your way to me here. I understand it must have taken some work on your part to track me down.
By Azura, if you have found this then you may have also found the scholar who possessed it?
Hello, outlander. Can I help you?
Be careful, outlander. I would never forgive myself if I inadvertently caused the death of two people. Please come see me in Suran so that I can be at ease.
Perhaps you have time to listen to my request now?
Muthsera, can you spare a moment?
Our ancestors speak through the Madstone. One day, I will speak through it too.

All Ahemmusa would wear the Madstone before being accepted as men and women in the tribe. Now that you bear it, our youth will travel to our ancient burial grounds to hear the voices of the ancestors.
Hearing the wailing of the ancestors is disquieting, even for us. It is difficult to focus while your ears ring with their cries.
You are worthy to carry the Madstone, Nerevarine.

You see the wind stir the grass and the hair on my head, %PCName. These things are full of life. But the winds of the moons stir the dead. On this wind unseen, the voices of our ancestors may cross the boundary between life and death. That is the power of the Madstone.
I watch the stables and take care of the Guars. That's it.

The Erabenimsun ashlander Adairen asked me to find Zuni, a friend who was exiled from the clan. She is supposedly sheltered within Maren Ancestral Tomb.

Zuni informed me that a nord named Batou also resides within the tomb, and appears to have been stealing her belongings. She gave me the key to Batou's vault, and told me I could take anything Batou allowed me to keep, as long as I looked for her other drum.

Good luck with whatever awaits you, outlander. You're certainly braver than I.
Ugh. I suppose I can't blame you, though. I'll just need to find a long enough rope, or perhaps the right kind of potion...
I'm glad to hear it, outlander! While you're down there, please let Zuni know I'm angry at her for leaving me alone up here.

After her exile, Zuni was in a rush to pack her things. She left behind one of her drums, and I intended to return it to her. I suppose you already know the rest. Would you be willing to bring the drum down to her on my behalf?
Adairen has always been an odd one, but she's been away from the camp more than usual since that mabrigash was exiled. I've heard she's sneaking off to that tomb west of us.
No time, no time... Of course, you're right. Down here, there is no time, is there?
The drum... Absolutely not, not! Drumbeats in the air, disturbing the peace! Thumping, thumping, never ending! So, of course, I ended it. No more thumping, thumping, THUMPING!
Such foolish foolishness! Can't you hear them? The townsfolk chattering around us, all throughout this endless night? Listen closely... Hear their wordless whispers, and join your voice with theirs!
After breaking into our fair city's vault, you would accuse this honorable guardsman of theft?! Not right, not right at all!
Halt, halt, halt! First that ominous beetle-elf, and now another strange character?! Citizens are not permitted to enter the Vault of Batou!
Hey, adventurer. What's brought you back down here?

Hey, adventurer. What's brought you back down here? Perhaps I'm mistaken, but you look like you aren't quite sure yourself.

Well, if you're trying to get back up, you've come to the right place.
Do be careful on the way out, adventurer. Despite my best efforts, there's still all sorts of things crawling around these old halls.

Aha... levitation trouble, adventurer? I promise it's not as intimidating as it seems. Just visualize your destination and mind your surroundings. Understood?

...Well, if not, I suppose you're in luck. I've prepared more potions than I know what to do with. They can't all be as well-crafted as the first one, though.

And now that those loose ends are tied up, I suppose you'll be on your way back. If she's still waiting around up there, could I ask that you pass this message along to Ada? I'm sure she'll be relieved to know I'm well, and I don't need her sending anymore helpful adventurers my way.

Oh? To be blunt with you, that's not what I expected to hear. He doesn't strike me as the type to be reasoned with, but perhaps that's simply an indication of your abilities. You have my gratitude, and Ada's as well.

Take this as a final reward from me. It isn't much, but it should get you out of here without any trouble.

A shame, but I suppose I figured as much. He didn't seem the type to be reasoned with. Perhaps I asked too much of you, or perhaps it was for the best. I can't say. What I can say is that you have my gratitude, and Ada's as well.

Here, a final reward from me. It isn't much, but it should get you out of here without any trouble.
Hah, you found my other drum! I must be repeating myself by now, but you have my thanks. How did your meeting with our mysterious Batou turn out?

Ah, so that was her excuse for bothering you. Thanks. I hope that my golems weren't too much of an obstacle, I know how agitated they get around people. No need to fret over these two, though. This mask lowers their guard quite effectively.

Hmm... I'd love to reward you for taking on this endeavor, but I'm afraid there's very little I can offer. That old Nord's locked himself away with half of my belongings.
My drum? I'm not sure what you're trying to prove, but it's nowhere to be seen.
Did you say Ada sent you?! I suspected her fear might get the better of her, but to send down a stranger in her place... I'm sorry for the trouble.
Well, I'm afraid you've reached the end of the pass.

Hello again, outlander.

I know I've already entrusted you with it, outlander, but do take care of Zuni's drum. It's very important to her.
What's brought you to this dusty place, outlander?

Curse you, Zuni... Why here, of all places?

Ah! Hello, outlander. Did you come from the camp?
The name's Zuni. I was a member of the Erabenimsun tribe, but seeing as I've been exiled, I'm here now. Not much else to tell.
Perhaps, calling it an "abyss" may seem dramatic, but surely you understand!

Honestly, it shouldn't even surprise me that someone like her would find comfort in a place like this. But how in the world am I supposed to visit someone who calls the bottom of a dark pit their home?! Not everyone is reckless enough to dive headlong into Azura-knows-what!

Ahem. I don't mean to subject you to my frustrations, outlander. But if you really do intend to continue on, could I ask for your assistance?

Glad to hear it. Here's that spare key, and, well... I'm sorry again for giving you more work. You seem like you can take care of yourself, but keep your guard up around Batou. It's not easy to get a read on him. Come on back here once it's dealt with.

So, are you in?

She's always been so stubborn about these things. I suppose I'll have to set aside my reservations and visit her. One of these days.

You say you returned the drum to her? Thank goodness, I'm so glad my worries were unfounded. Ah, did she tell you anything?
I swear, the next time I see her...

The Twin Lamps were disturbed that one of thier own members would resort to something so vile to fight slavery. Still they are glad that I didn't tell House Telvanni about the incident as it would drastically hurt thier cause.

Hopefully they won't get any crazy ideas.
Thanks for informing us about this matter.

I'll also let the rest of house telvanni know of your report. They shouldn't be as reluctant to speak with you anymore.
I'm glad you told us about this. The Baram Family can rest easily now.
We heard about the incident. Even though we weren't directly affected, House Dres is grateful.

We are many. We are the bones and spirits of the ancestor dead, amalgamated and set to task. We are guardians, teachers, the first step between those gone and those who remain. We are oft called Bonelords, though this is a meagre descriptor, ill suited to the depth of the truth. We tend to the tomb here, and the tomb beyond the waking eye and mortal time.
We are assembled from this many, a host of spirits are refined and merged into this shell to better suit our ordained guardianship. We are amalgam, many voices bound to many bones.

We are the sacred dead. Our bones are taken from warriors, priests, scholars, hearth keepers and those who would serve in honourable death. From each only the bones deemed worthy are taken and the rest given over to the Ghostfence. We are then purified in flame, blessed by the Three.

A bit of a swit, if well meaning. They are a knight of the Resolute of Zenithar, sworn to protect the hard working citizens and this ordained venture. Their words, not mine. They rent my attic room, paid for a considerable time up front. I asked him to investigate the nearby tomb when the nightmares first started, but he has not returned yet.
His home is yours, for the years left on his lease.
A pity, he was a good man even if he was a little uptight about his oaths.
This name means nothing to us. Perhaps they were the one who came before.
Bound to foul service, now free to whatever fate awaits those who do not embrace the Three and find themselves destined for the Ghostfence. Pitiable.
Elmussa Damori is suffering from some kind of Dunmer curse, hasn't slept well in days.
You are unwelcome here, this place has fallen under the sway of evil. Begone, before we are forced to unthether your spirit from the flesh and the bone, by blade and by claw.

One who twists the arts of death to foul purpose has stolen into the grand hall and is enacting an unclean rite, tethering us all to their will. I hear the others, those without form, and they are suffering. I was commanded to forsake my duty and stand guard. They commanded nothing of defending with claw and blade, and less yet of singing through the blood to call on those who would answer. We would have you bring the justice of blades and teeth and blood to the necromancer. Do this, for the dead.
Useless creature.
If you will not help, begone.

I see you through the eyes of the spirit, and the echo of the words in your thoughts. Guard your Ancestors from beasts, from thieves, from profane priest and sorcerers. Let no creature steal your spirits, for the plundered hearth is diminished, and the plundered tomb is shamed. Those were my words, sent through the blood and lineage to find one who might purge this place before it is further profaned. You are yet another who has arrived in their stead. We are the Gravetender.
We are the door through the wall of the world. We are the road, the Wisdom and the Power.
Honor the Ancestors upon your hearths, within your halls, in the community of your temples, in the solitude of your tombs.
Live in One World with your spirits. Honor the spirits within and without you. Do not grieve for us. Take shelter in our arms, and pay heed to our words.

In the last few nights it has been getting more strained, desperate. I hear them in the day now, faintly, from every dark corner and empty space. I know an omen from the ancestors when I cross one. I may not be the most devout, but by the Three I know this needs to be dealt with.
Go to the tomb, find whatever evil is disturbing the ancestors and destroy it. I sent Cedric Tratoris to investigate, but he has not returned. Can you help me? You will be paid for the work.
Go to the Indalen ancestral tomb to the north-east of here, find whatever is calling to me in my dreams and make it stop.
Then leave me be, I will find another.
The situation resolved itself, the dreams stopped suddenly. I need no help.
The dreams changed, and then stopped. I need no help it seems.

So you have heard of my predicament. Every time I sleep I see visions of this screaming horror made of bones and souls, and this voice quoting the Doors of the Spirit. 
Guard your Ancestors from beasts, from thieves, from profane priest and sorcerers. Let no creature steal your spirits, for the plundered hearth is diminished, and the plundered tomb is shamed.
Over and over it chants at me, pointing, accusing. I want it to stop.
I felt it, a great silence descended and my suffering has eased. Thank you.

I felt them, a chorus of praises and gratitudes that my duty was fulfilled. Thank you for doing this. Since Cedric will not be needing it I would offer you use of the loft for the remaining time on his lease as proper reward for your effort.
I felt a great severing, as if something wounded me in my heart. Then the presence haunting me faded. Thank you.
No new nightmares, it seems the problem is gone completely.
Have you gone to the tomb yet? Nothing has changed.

You have fulfilled the duty, we shall end our song to the blood. They may rest now, we will be silent as the dead ought to be. Be glad mortal you cannot hear the screams, the foul defilers soul is being dismantled to empower the wards upon this place at this very moment, as is good and right under the judgement of the Three. The ending of the words is Almsivi.

I intended no harm beyond what any might endure for their kin. They are a descendant of one interred here, knowing or otherwise, and there is a duty to be fulfilled. If it means anything to you I grant you all of our apologies to carry to them, hollow as it is.

Ygfa says that her friend, Piernette Beluelle, had a silver bowl stolen. She gave me directions to her friend's house starting from the north entrance to the Foreign Quarter of Vivec. Due north from the bridge to the Foreign Quarter of Vivec is an east-west bridge across a lagoon. Cross the bridge east, then follow the path as it heads north. Pass Nilera's farmhouse on the left, and the next house north will be Piernette's farmhouse.

My friend, Piernette Beluelle, had a silver bowl stolen. This must be the same one. You must go speak with Piernette. Best if you start from a familiar landmark -- the north entrance to the Foreign Quarter of Vivec. Due north from the bridge to the Foreign Quarter of Vivec is an east-west bridge across a lagoon. Cross the bridge east, then follow the path as it heads north. You'll pass Nilera's farmhouse on the left, and the next house north will be Piernette's farmhouse.

This is Vassir-Didanat Ebony Mine. I'm the supervisor here, I make sure things run smoothly and that all the Ebony is collected, processed and then sold. So far we've not had any trouble in that regard.
Here you go. Get well soon.

I discovered a small island near Solstheim. Despite fresh northern winds, it reeks of the rotten flesh and I can hear the wailing of the undead trapped below its surface.
I have found an enchanted stone talisman, it can teleport me somewhere on the island.
I managed to find all the Fingerbone Keys and open the door.
I have defeated a powerful necromancer who lived in the tomb.
Berandas Transformed

I found the journal of a dead mage deep below Berandas. They present an interesting theory as to what might be the cause of Berandas' daedric corruption. Perhaps I should bring the journal to that Medila person that the mage keeps mentioning. Based on what I read I should probably check the Caldera Mages Guild.

When I told Medila about the mage's theory according to which the Boots of the Apostle are responsible for the daedric corruption that has befallen Berandas she was startled. According to her, it is not conclusive as no buildings have leapt into the air since I have brought the boots with me. I guess i can see her point. She says she wants to conduct further research herself. For now, the reason for Berandas' transformation shall remain a mystery to me.

When I told Medila about the mage's theory according to which the Boots of the Apostle are responsible for the daedric corruption that has befallen Berandas she seemed startled. She seemed even more startled when she learned that I didn't recover the boots. She insulted me and ended the conversation. I am getting the feeling the journal's author may have misplaced her affection. I suppose I will never learn for certain what the reason for Berandas' transformation is.

Medila doesn't seem particularly concerned for who I assumed was her friend. I declined to tell her what the mage had found out, but when she offered me a decent amount of money in exchange for the journal, I couldn't resist. For now, Berandas' transformation shall remain a mystery to me.

Medila doesn't seem particulary concerned for who I assumed was her friend. She doesn't even remember the mage's name. I declined to tell her about what the mage had found out. Medila offered me money in exchange for the journal, but I resisted. Clearly the mage had misplaced her affection. It would appear that both her name and the definitive reason for Berandas' corruption will remain a mystery to me.
Hello there, %PCRace, what can I do for ... wait, I know that book.
I told you, I don't have time for idiocy.
I will find out what has happened to Berandas myself. Please leave.
Get out of my sight!
I have what I need. Now, go away.

You didn't recover the boots? Moron. How can you not recover them when you're down there anyway? Aren't you curious? Get out of my sight, I don't have time for idiocy. I will find out what is going on in Berandas myself.

Well, have any buildings risen in your wake? Have any castles displayed the urge to leap into the sky? ... Didn't think so. No, there must be something else going on. I will find out myself. Now, please leave me alone. You have been utterly useless.

The Boots of the Apostle? You mean the very same boots that Tiber Septim supposedly used to fly down from the mountains? That's just ... that's lunacy. And even if it were true ... even if the boots really were down there ... it's impossible for them to make entire structures rise upward. I mean ... did you recover the boots?
What? That doesn't make any sense. Wait, what boots?
Then what are you still doing here? Get out of my sight!
You drive a hard bargain. Here's your gold. Now give me that and get lost, will you?
Fine. 1000 drakes. Last offer.
Great. Now if you would, I have other things to attend to.
Excellent. Now if you'll excuse me, I have work to do.
Then perhaps I can persuade you to give me the journal? It should go to the guild anyway. 200 drakes?
Aw, that's cute. Yes, that one has always been a simpleton. Well, was she at least able to find out the cause of the daedric corruption? Or were you?
Fascinating. And what about ... uh ... you know ... her? You bringing back her journal instead of herself is probably not the best of signs ...

Oh, you went to Berandas, and so did she. Interesting. Didn't think she had it in her. She was always babbling about Berandas and about how she wanted to find out what transpired there, with those daedric structures bursting through the ground. Well, so we have been told, but I haven't actually seen it. Is it true then? Have daedric structures risen from the deep and claimed Berandas?

Yes, I've seen it before. It's a journal. It belongs to ... what was her name again? That Dunmer girl always running around trying to impress me. Sorry, I'm blanking on it. Anyway, where did you find it?
I'm Malus Sarobar, I'm the master of this mine. Foreman too. So kindly leave, I'm quite busy.
Treasure of Olmgerd the Outlaw
I found the remains of Olmgerd the Outlaw and looted both his armor and Stormkiss.
Researcher's Request
An Altmer named Egard is looking for a research assistant to collect samples from Hawia egg mine.
Egard needs five fresh kwama eggs for his studies.
Now Egard want's five samples each of scrib jelly and kwama cuttle.
The last thing Egard needs is five pieces of kwama chitin.
I have gathered everything Egard needs for his studies and he rewarded me with several useful potions.
Missing Miners
The foreman of Hawia, Raththen, has asked for help in locating a group of missing egg miners.
I've agreed to help Raththen locate the missing miners. I should ask around and see if anyone else saw them the day they went missing.
Apparently the three miners went into the tunnels to find the kwama queen.
I found the bodies of the missing miners near the entrance of the queen's lair. They were trampled to death by the warriors that guard her.

I've informed Raththen of the fate of the missing miners. He has given me a reward and offered me a job here any time I want to mine for eggs. For each crate I bring him I will receive forty-five septems.

Trampled to death you say? A terrible fate... Regardless, you did what I asked. I hope you'll find this fair payment. Plenty more where that came from if you'd like to work here as an egg miner. As you know I’m in need of some replacements. I’ll pay you forty-five drakes for each crate of eggs you bring me, now that’s a fair deal at eighteen eggs a crate.
Then if you will excuse me I have to get back to counting eggs.

Great, I'm usually stuck up here operating this crane and shipping eggs to the top, so I dont really get to see what goes on in the tunnels. Maybe one of the other miners can tell you more. Now if you will excuse me I have to get back to counting eggs. Come back to me if you find anything.
Did you change your mind?

If I remember it was a Khajiit named Jo'sasha, a Redguard named Daroman, and an Orc whos name I can't recall.  All I know is they came in on a Morndas for work and never left that evening. Egg mining can be dangerous buisness, they could have all fallen into an acid pit or been eaten alive by foragers. I just find it odd they all went missing at the same time. Do you think you can assist me in finding them? I'll pay you.
Never heard of 'em.
Sorry, they worked on the opposite end of the mine. I barely ran into them.
Yeah, I saw them all heading off into the tunnels together. Second tunnel on the right if you go down this ridge, the one with two torches.

Ah, sweet Sillapi. Nothing better to soothe a cough. Yeah I saw them the day they went missing. They said they were going to find the queen or something like that. I guess they thought it would be an easy spot to grab some eggs.
Don't play dumb with me. You want information, give me the Sillapi.
You got the Sillapi?
I might help you if you help me. Bring me a Silapi from Gren, you can find him in the shack over there.
What do you need it for?
Take what? Come back when you actually have some.
Gren has the key to the storage shed. It's where we cure the century eggs.
Secrets for Sillapi?
Honest pay for honest work.
Come back when you have a full crate. That's eighteen eggs, and I only take the large ones.
Here you go my friend.
Not enough here to make Sillapi the way I do it.

Egg-scellent! Ha-ahem... Yes, well then. The next thing I need you to collect is five handfulls each of kwama cuttle and scrib jelly. A good source of these can be found in the kwama cocoons. This is where the larva scrib goes through metamorphosis and changes into either a forager or a grubber. Aren't kwama just fascinating? I do enjoy observing them, from a distance of course. The cocoons can be difficult to get to so I'm going to give you a few levitation potions. Use them wisely.
What are you waiting for? Please hurry.
I see you've got the eggs, are you ready to give them to me?
Where are the eggs I asked for? Come back when you have them.
What do you want, n'wah?
Got any eggs for me?
Find anything yet?
I still need help finding those miners.

Haven't I seen you down here before? You were helping that Altmer that was camping out down here, right? You seem to know your way around these mines. Look, I need a little help and I'm too busy to look into it myself. A group of miners went missing down here recently, they were all new hires who lived in the foreign quarter. One day they just never left the mines and I have yet to see them since. I need someone to go into these tunnels and try to find them.
Welcome to Hawia.
Been mining eggs my whole life, ever since I was a little scrib stomper. I've always been the best at it. That's why they made me foreman.
I've been down in this egg mine longer than anyone else, for the longest time it was just me and Raththen down here.

I have been a traveling botanist and biologist for many years now, I go to the far corners of every province and pasture to procure the rarest ingredients. I make my way by selling the potions I create myself, i've become quite proficient over the years.
I'm the foreman of Hawia egg mines. I keep track of everything coming in and going out.

I make the best Sillapi to ever cross your lips, my own recipe. Just three simple ingredients. One large kwama egg, some cuttle and a little jelly. You bring me all three and I can make a fresh batch any time. Gives you some energy after you've been hauling eggs all day.

I'm an alchemist and biologist. I’ve come to Hawia egg mine to study the kwama first hand. Their eggs are famous across Tamriel and I have always been fascinated by the origin of this miracle food. I've seen some illustrations but I have to admit they are not how I expected them, much larger than I imagined. Research has gone well viewing their habits from afar, but I’ve run into a bit of a problem and the local miners are unwilling to provide any assistance to an outlander. All I ask for is a few samples.

Good enough, I'll be crushing them into a powder anyway. You did a good job, %PCName. I've enjoyed my time here in Hawia but I'm ready to head back to my lab for analysis. Before I go, here is your reward.
I promise this is the last thing I need from you. I have plenty more potions to give you if you finish the job.
Have you managed to find any chitin? I hope you didn't have to fight too hard for it.

I can't wait to get back to the lab and anaylize these! Well done. There is one last thing I need for my studies. I just need five good pieces of kwama chitin. They might not be willing to give it up so easily, but you may be able to find some abandoned husks if you travel deeper into the mines. I have a few potions to give you now, and more later if you complete the task.
There should be plenty in these mines, keep looking.
Do you have the cuttle and jelly?
Would you be interested in being my assistant? I don't have much money but I can reward you with a few useful potions I brewed myself. What do you say?

I promise to reward your efforts handsomly. The first thing I need is five fresh kwama eggs. I would collect them myself but I am petrefied by the way they scream. I'm going to send you off with some antidote that should null the effects of their poision. Off you go now.
Come back if you change your mind.
Have you reconsidered my offer?

I talked to Antjurah Drethos in Gnaar Mok. She came all the way from the mainland to find out about her ancestors and asked me to enter her family's Ancestral Tomb and bring back any clue that might tell her what her ancestors lived through. Drethos Ancestral Tomb can be found east of Gnaar Mok, just along the road.

I talked to Antjurah Drethos in Gnaar Mok. She came all the way from the mainland to find out about her ancestors and asked me to enter her family's Ancestral Tomb and bring back any clue that might tell her what her ancestors lived through. I told her I am not interested to help her.

Deep within Drethos Ancestral Tomb I found two dead lovers frozen in time. One had an ornate dagger thrust through the heart. I tried to take it, but it was stuck. When I touched it an ancient Lich appeared out of nowhere and attacked me. After I defeated it I was able to take the dagger. This might be the sort of thing that Antjurah asked for. However, I feel the dagger must have a deeper meaning. I should look around and see if it has a special use.

When I touched it an ancient Lich appeared out of nowhere and attacked me. After I defeated it I was able to take the dagger. There must be a deeper meaning behind this. I should look around and see if there is a special use for the dagger.

Behind the big stone door I met an Ancestor Ghost who seemed lost and confused. It spoke of pain and light and punishment. I believe it may have been one of the two skeletal lovers, but whether it was the stabber or the stabbed I cannot tell. When I told it that it was free it put an enchantment on the dagger.

Behind the big stone door I met an Ancestor Ghost who seemed lost and confused. It spoke of pain and light and punishment. I believe it may have been one of the two skeletal lovers, but whether it was the stabber or the stabbed I cannot tell. When I proclaimed that it deserved its punishment it attacked. It posed little threat to me, but with its last breath it put an enchantment on the Ardor Knife that might make using the blade ... risky. I don't think I will ever truly know what happened in this tomb.
The ghost teleported me back to the tomb's entrance. When I materialized it was gone. I don't think I will ever find out what truly happened in this tomb.
