The ghost teleported me back to the tomb's entrance. When I materialized it was gone. I don't think I will ever find out what truly happened in this tomb. Still, I should return to Antjurah and tell her what little I have learned.
I reported back to Antjurah Drethos. She was grateful for everything I could tell her and rewarded me with gold. The Ardor Knife is now mine.
Yes, you did what I asked of you. You have my thanks!

I believe I promised you a reward for running my little errand. Whatever I can offer will seem pale in comparison to the Ardor Knife, still, we had an agreement. Please take these coins, may they help you in your future endeavours. Thank you for giving me some insight into my family's past. It seems it is a sad one, but then again, death always is. Isn't it?

Oh no, that blade is not meant for me. My ancestors kept it from their descendants for a reason. It belongs to you now, you who were brave enough to best the challenges of root and rock, of bone and death.
A fascinating find. It appears to be of magnificent craftsmanship. It is disturbing that it was used in such a violent act. Then again, we do not know what truly transpired, do we?

The two people buried there must have been my ancient forefathers. Perhaps the very people who built the tomb. As to the ancestor ghost you met ... I'm afraid I do not know more than you.  What about the Ardor Knife?

Intriguing. I told you my family was once rich and powerful. From what you're telling me it seems they put their wealth to good use when building the tomb. It saddens me to see it in such a poor state. And yet, perhaps it is fitting. Even that which is meant to preserve the dead is ultimately subject to death and decay.
You have been to Drethos Ancestral Tomb? And what did you find?
I guess I will have to look for someone else then.
I will eagerly wait for your return!
Too bad. I guess I will have to look for an adventurer who is more daring than you.

Excellent! The Drethos Ancestral Tomb lies only a short way to the east of Gnaar Mok. It shouldn't be hard to find. Be careful when you go in there! And please bring back to me any clue to the past that you might find.

I am not skilled in anything that would help me conquer those ancient depths. But looking at you, I feel that you might be up to the task. Perhaps you could enter the tomb and uncover its mysteries? I promise I will make it worth your while. I might not be as rich and powerful as my ancestors, but there are still a few resources left to me. What say you, %PCRace?

I crave for some sort of connection to my past, however distant it may be. There is an old Ancestral Tomb, not too far from this village. My ancestors built it long ago. I wish to find out who is buried there. And I wish to find out about their story. However, the locals tell me that particular tomb is completely overgrown with vegetation and thus very difficult and dangerous to traverse. And the Undead roaming the ancient halls make entering the tomb even more perilous.

Well, it's actually more than just a little errand. You see, I have come all the way here from the mainland to find out about my ancestors. Not much is left of my kin. In fact, as far as I know, I am the last member of the Drethos family. We were once a household name, very rich and powerful, but all of that is long gone. Now it is just me and I fear that when I leave this world the Drethos name will truly be forgotten for all eternity.
You have returned! How did it go? Did you run a little errand for me?
To the light ...
I ... wait ...
To touch ... the light ...
Thank you ... my love ... now come ... to touch ... the light ...
I ... curse ... you ...
My love ... gone ... and I could not ... bear ... my body ... my soul ... torn ... lost ... and you ... you were bound ... to ...
Light ... always in the light ... to see ... but never feel ... never touch ... only ... a memory ... a punishment ...
The Ardor Knife ... it twisted ... it sealed ... it released ... I remember ... pain ... unspeakable ... pain ... and then I was ... here ...
You ... are ... not ...
I ... we ... we were in love ... and you ... you were ... my everything ... do you not ... remember?
You came ... my love ... after all this time ...
Back again, %PCRace? I doubt we will have much to talk about.
Hello again, %PCRace! Ready for your expedition to Drethos Ancestral Tomb?

Greetings, %PCRace, my name is Antjurah Drethos. Do you have business in Gnaar Mok or are you just passing through? If you're staying in the vicinity, perhaps I could persuade you to run a little errand for me? I would offer you proper compensation, of course.

I've been tending to this lighthouse in Dagon Fel for some years now. We Nords built it here to improve the safety of seatrade around the Sea of Ghosts. Ships towns across Morrowind and Skyrim dock here for trading. The beacon guides ships to a safe passage into the bay, but those blasted menhirs are still a real menace around here.
Welcome to Dagon Fel, %PCRace. My name is Vigunn and I'm the lighthouse keeper of this town.
Good to see you again, %PCRace. Did you want to ask something about the town of Dagon Fel or this northern lighthouse?
Yeah, that's me. I'm the lighthouse keeper of Dagon Fel.
Vigunn is the lighthouse keeper of this town. You can find him up in his lighthouse on north-west side of town.

Hello %PCRace, I'm Aras Favel, lighthouse keeper by profession. I keep the beacon lit so ships can navigate safely to the city of Vivec. The water around here can be very treacherous, even with a fire guiding the way.
Isn't she a beauty? I've been maintaining her, as lighthouse keeper, for so many years now. I Actually lost count.
I am %name. I serve as commandant and Chapter Steward of this garrison.
I am a Skaal Honor Guard.
The Secret of Bethamez

I accepted a request from Hetman Abelmawia in Gnisis to explore the Dwemer ruin of Bethamez beneath Gnisis Eggmine. Ever since it was uncovered the mine has been shaken by tremors, and Hetman wants me to find a clue as to what might be the cause. He recommends I bring a few potions of levitation. When down there I should look for anything that might tell me what is going on, like notes or schematics.
Hetman Abelmawia in Gnisis asked me to figure out what is causing the tremors that have been disturbing egg production in Gnisis eggmine. I declined his request.

I found some old schematics in Bethamez. I can't read them because they are in Dwemer script, but the images appear to depict a large machine that somehow seems to be able to divert lava currents. And I think I also found the particular machine ... I should return to Hetman Abelmawia and report my findings.

Since neither of us can read Dwemer script Hetman has asked me to go to Arvs-Drelen and talk to Baladas Demnevanni, a Telvanni wizard with a great interest in everything Dwarven. I am to ask him to confirm our suspicions as to what the machine does. Hopefully, he can tell me how to deactivate it.

Baladas confirmed that the machine diverts lava currents. It might even be powerful enough to suck in magma from Red Mountain. He told me how to deactivate the machine or at least slow it down enough to stop the tremors: I need to find a powered Dwemer Coherer and use it to extract the machine's power core. Baladas thinks that the only place to do that is very deep below the Earth at the machine's heart. He gave me some explosives to get there.

I extracted the power core. I don't think the machine shut down completely, but based on the noises I am fairly certain that the lava currents are slowing down. Hopefully, this will put an end to the tremors. I should return to Baladas and give him the power core, just as I promised.

Baladas seemed glad that I brought him the power core. He believes the machine will keep running on low capacity for an indefinite amount of time, but confirmed that the tremors should stop now. He speculated in regards to the machine's purpose and had some ... eye-opening ideas. I should return to Hetman Abelmawia and tell him that I solved the problem.

Hetman Abelmawia was happy about my report. He is confident that the eggmine will soon go back to its former level of productivity. As a reward, he gave me a Dwemer artifact that the people he first sent into the ruin brought back.
The tremors have stopped. Things should turn back to normal now. I am sure we will soon reclaim this part of the mine.

Careful, stranger. The Kwama are agitated. I recommend you don't visit the western parts of the cave. We certainly don't. Not at the moment. We abandoned this entire part of the mine because the Kwama are going wild. It's the tremors. Damn those old Dwemer. Whatever they did down there, it's causing trouble, all these millenia later.
Now that the tremors have stopped productivity should go up again. And perhaps in time, the Kwama that are with the queen will calm down.

Yes, we have had trouble here lately. The earth has been shaking and the Kwama don't like that. We don't like it. It's the ruin, the Dwemer ruin down below. Bethamez they call it. Wish I knew what was going on there, but it's too dangerous. Some of us climbed down to do some digging, but none of us can deal with a Dwemer Centurion. Someone else will have to go down there. Someone who is a capable fighter. Or who knows how to sneak past ...
I think we concluded our business.

Anyway, I wish to inspect the power core now. If my suspicions are correct, it is a supercooled superconductor designed to store and then release large amounts of energy in the form of heat. It might be just what I need for my new ...
I wonder ... perhaps it is part of some overly ambitious terraforming project. Or maybe it is just a fancy heating device. Who knows ...
Just as well. Whatever it may be, I believe the machine can run on low capacity even without the power core for a long time.  But at least the tremors should stop now.
Yes, yes, you're a sweetheart. Here are 10 drakes for your troubles. Have you ever found out what the ultimate purpose of that machine was? I mean beyond moving lava. What is moving lava good for?
Do you have it? The power core? Give it to me!
Go ... go, and bring me that power core!
Rocks? What are rocks to me? Take this and blow them apart!

You might need a powered Dwemer Coherer to extract the core. If you can't find one, perhaps you can take a depleted one and recharge it at a power station. There might be one down there. Oh, also, I don't know where you found this schematic, but it seems certain to me that you will have to delve deeper into the ruin. According to these schematics, the power core is located very deep below the earth, at the machine's heart. Place the powered coherer in the opening mechanism and the core will appear.

Great! Then just ... get the core. If you retrieve it from the machine, it should shut down. Or at least its energy level will decrease so much that the lava currents will slow down significantly. I suspect that will stop the tremors.
The machine's core. The power core. I want it, I need it. Do you agree? I will tell you all you need to know.

What is that, show me that! Mmmhh ... fascinating. Yes, you might be quite right. That machine does appear to be wondrous. Clearly, it sucks in all the surrounding lava. I can't be sure, but the device might even be powerful enough to divert large amounts of magma from Red Mountain. No wonder there are tremors. What an ingenious people the Dwemer were. Well, it should be quite simple to deactivate it, if you know how. However, I will not tell you. Unless, of course, you give me what I want.

Tremors you say? In the eggmine? What is it to me? I don't rely on those egg miners. Although I do admit, they can be quite delicious every once in a while. The eggs, that is, not the miners. What do you want?
I appreciate all that you have done for us!
Now the mine can hopefully resume full productivity. Thank you, %PCName!
The men I first sent to investigate the Dwemer ruin found this and brought it to me. It's a bit rusty, but perhaps you will have use for it.
Astounding work! Thank you for taking care of this. I don't have much that I can give you, but perhaps ...
What did Baladas say? Have you been able to solve the issue?
Please go to Arvs-Drelen and talk to the Telvanni wizard Baladas Demnevanni. We must know how to deactivate the machine.

That sounds ominous. If that is indeed what is causing the tremors, we must deactivate the machine. Unfortunately, I cannot read Dwemer script. However, there might be someone in Gnisis who can. We usually try not to bother him, he can be very ... eccentric. But I think we have no choice. Please go to Arvs-Drelen and talk to the Telvanni wizard Baladas Demnevanni. He is very interested in Dwarven history and machinery. Perhaps he will be able to tell us what we must do.
Have you found anything?
Please report back to me as soon as you find anything that might give us a clue as to what is happening within that ruin.
I am disappointed to hear that.

Excellent. I suggest you get a few levitation potions before you go down there. Climbing back out will be a lot harder than climbing down. And here, you'll need this key. The Imperial Legion has ordered that no one except the workers be permitted inside, but you will be there under my orders, so there should be no trouble. Please report back to me as soon as you find anything that might give us a clue as to what is happening within that ruin.

They swear they touched nothing, but ever since then the mine has been plagued by tremors. Kwama don't like tremors, and neither do my workers. As a result, egg production has decreased significantly. Say, you look as though you can take care of yourself. If you are daring enough, would you go down to the Dwemer ruin of Bethamez and investigate what the cause of these tremors is? If we knew what it was, perhaps we could put an end to it.

Yes, we have had some problems down there lately. Ever since we uncovered that Dwemer ruin, that wretched place. As far as we can tell it is completely destroyed and dead. It opens up to a huge hole as if everything just sank into the ground. Some of us climbed down there, but quickly came back when they encountered a Dwemer Centurion.
The tremors have stopped. I wonder what happened.

There are rumors, yes. The Legion are a secretive bunch, they don't tell us anything. But we can feel it. There is a rumbling coming from beneath the earth. It's very weak up here on the surface, but I bet there is something happening in the eggmine. Perhaps Hetman Abelmawia knows more. He is usually in the know about all things concerning the mine.

I reported to Almalexia that Salas Valor is dead, and that any threat he represented to the peace of Mournhold is now eliminated. She was pleased, and rewarded me with a special divine blessing and the permission to wear Ordinator armor.

I reported to Almalexia that Salas Valor is dead, and that any threat he represented to the peace of Mournhold is now eliminated. She was pleased, and offered to reward me with a special divine blessing and the permission to wear Ordinator armor. I declined her blessing, however, and I think she was less pleased by that.

Drin asks that I use blessed oil to cleanse this shrine and restore its power. I will first have to rid the area of all of the Profane, powerful liches who draw strength from the power of the Shrine of the Dead. When they are destroyed, I can cleanse the shrine. I should enter the sewers from the Temple basement. Once there, I will need to head east through the old Temple Gardens, then south to find the Shrine of the Dead.
I have succeeded in cleansing the shrine.
Gavas Drin was pleased, and a bit surprised, at the news I was able to restore the shrine. He has presented me with a Blessed Spear, a gift from the Lady Almalexia.
Garil Varis says his son, Trels Varis, is a scholar in a private Temple school in Kragenmoor, out west near Cyrodiil.

Marena Varis says she has no idea where Trels Varis is right now, but Garil Varis says his son, Trels Varis, is a scholar in a private Temple school in Kragenmoor. It doesn't make sense that the father knows but the mother doesn't. I mentioned this peculiarity to Garil Varis, and he said Marena is getting old and forgetful. But I suspect they are not telling me the truth.
Marena Varis says she has a son named Trels Varis, but she hasn't seen him recently and has no idea where he is right now.

Garil Varis says his son, Trels Varis, is a scholar in a private Temple school in Kragenmoor, but Marena Varis says she has no idea where Trels Varis is right now. It doesn't make sense that the father knows but the mother doesn't. I mentioned this peculiarity to Marena Varis, and she said Garil would forget his head if it weren't jammed tight on his neck. But I suspect they are not telling me the truth.
I told someone about the death of a Tribunal god. They did not believe me and took offense at the suggestion that such a thing could occur.

I suspect Marena and Garil Varis are not telling me the truth about their son, Trels Varis. But it gives me an idea. If I threaten to hurt Marena and Garil, it may persuade Trels Varis to stop printing lies about King Helseth in 'The Common Tongue'.
You've found the Mazed Band? Amazing... Almalexia will want to hear about this immediately. You are to speak with her directly. I hope you realize what an honor you're receiving, %PCName.

All I know is that the goddess wants it returned. You'll find it in the ruins beneath the Temple. Search to the northwest in the sewers in the Abandoned Crypt. As for the item itself, I don't really see why you'd need to know any more about it. Gavas Drin could tell you more...were he not dead.

All I know is that the goddess wants it returned. You'll find it in the ruins beneath the Temple. Search to the northwest in the sewers in the Abandoned Crypt. As for the item itself, I don't really see why you'd need to know any more about it. If you must inquire, perhaps Gavas Drin can give you more details.
Go there and anoint the shrine.

When the Shrine was created, it was anointed with blessed oil from the time of the Armistice. Re-anointing the Shrine with the same oil again will reforge the original bond it once had. The Shrine is protected by the Profane, powerful liches who feed from the power of the shrine and must be destroyed for the cleansing to work. Do not misplace this oil. Sourcing additional bottles may be impossible.
I am no mystic, but a weaponsmith: the finest in all Bamz-Amschend. That blade shows supreme craftsmanship, but it's lacking something. I believe with a little work, I could add fire to that blade.

[Almalexia regards you coolly.] Perhaps you think yourself too proud to accept the gifts of your Mistress? Very well. It is as you wish. At the very least, you may now wear the armor of the Ordinators freely throughout Morrowind.
I bless you with my gift, and mark you as my own. You may now wear the armor of the Ordinators freely throughout Morrowind. Be ever faithful in your service, and you may expect more generous rewards.

Salas Valor is dead? The pain is almost more than I can bear... but you have served me faithfully, and it is in my mind to grant you a divine blessing. Would you like skin as tough as iron? Would you like my protection against paralyzing and poisonous terror? Or would you wish to always bask in warm comfort of my reflected glory? Quick, now! Choose! You must not keep your Deity waiting!

Salas Valor is already dead? The pain is almost more than I can bear... but somehow, you have anticipated my need and served me faithfully! It is a sign! This miracle compels me to grant you a divine blessing.  Would you like skin as tough as iron? Would you like my protection against paralyzing and poisonous terror? Or would you wish to always bask in warm comfort of my reflected glory? Quick, now! Choose! You must not keep your Deity waiting!
My wife says she doesn't know where he is? Well, Marena is getting right forgetful in her old age. Of course Trels is in Kragenmoor, like I said.

Hmm. I don't know anyone by that name. But wait a minute, and let me think.... You know, maybe he's one of the Varis brood. I thought they had all left Mournhold to seek their fortunes in the outside world. Impressive bunch of kids, they were -- smart and ambitious. But maybe you should ask Marena Varis or Garil Varis up at the Temple. Maybe they'll know.
You have your blade. Now leave me in peace.
Have you found the Pyroil Tar?
...is someone there?
I see you've obtained Barilzar's Mazed Band. We have much to discuss.

Well. I must say, you've done your research. You've located Marena and Garil Varis. I value truth -- but I value the lives of my parents more highly. Very well. I will not discuss King Helseth in 'The Common Tongue'. You have my word. And now, if you'll excuse me, we'll have to relocate immediately, now that the secret of our office is spoiled.
I have used the tar. My service to you has ended.
Where is the blade?

Let me show you how a true Dwemer craftsman works... and now I am finished. Make good use of this blade, Dwemer. I do not know where you found such a fine blade, but I am proud to have helped make it even better. If you'll excuse me, I feel exhausted after this...
When applied to Dwemer metal it can remain aflame indefinitely. This should turn your blade from a mundane piece of metal into a true work of art.
An old Daedric ruin. And a great source of Pyroil Tar.

Deep, deep caves. An old Daedric ruin. The bones and blood of ancient creatures here congealed into tar. I remember finding some through a cave-in at the Passage of the Walker. I've sent a request to get it cleaned up but I have not yet received a response.Take care down there, young Dwemer.
It's now a one-of-a-kind piece of art.
I require the Pyroil Tar, first.
My workshop is well stocked -- I only lack Pyroil Tar. You can find it in the lower caves of Norenen-dur, in the Citadel of Myn Dhrur. It's an old ruin far beneath Bamz-Amschend.

Sounds like Larrius Varro alright. Sends half the garrison off to find some ragged bandit stealing fish from swamp peasants, and meanwhile the Thieves' Guild is ruining business in Balmora and he does nothing. Typical.

I'm sorry, %PCName, it would compromise my cover if I tried to help. You might try talking to the Thieves Guild, or maybe the Imperial Magistrate over at Fort Moonmoth. Rumour has it Nolus Atrius is as crooked as a barrel of fish hooks, and rumour's not wrong. Or if you have friends in the Great Houses, maybe they could pull some strings for you.

Nonsense. Officially, you're as upstanding a citizen as anyone in the Empire. I couldn't possibly comment on what you do away from the eyes of the law, of course, but I'm sure your business is all perfectly above board. Right?
Unfortunate. Well, that's your choice. Let me know if you change your mind
Excellent. I'll take care of everything. Consider it done, in fact. How's that for Imperial efficiency, eh?
Smart thinking, %PCRace, but you don't have the gold to cover that. Come back to me when you do.

So. You've been expelled from the House, and now you're on the outs with the law as well. Such good judgement you show, %PCName. I'm afraid I can't help you with this one. Go make amends with the House, if you can, and then we'll talk business.

Fallen afoul of Imperial law, %PCRank? And now you need help. I understand. Perhaps I could help, but I wouldn't want to think I was encouraging criminality. I would need some proof that you're a reformed character. Perhaps a donation of %CrimeGoldDiscount drakes to the Hlaalu Veterans and Widows fund would be convincing.
Fallen afoul of Imperial law, %PCRace? I'm sorry to hear that. But I'm not sure what you think I can do about it.

Been having trouble with the law, %PCRank? [He looks amused] Irritating s'wits. Life would be much easier if everyone did things the Telvanni way. If you've got %CrimeGoldDiscount drakes to spare, I can save you the bother of dealing with it yourself.

You've been falsely accused of a crime? Horrendous. Where does the Legion find these incompetents? Now, don't worry, you've come to the right man, %PCName. I'd never stand for such a miscarriage of justice. We can sort this out quite easily. If you have, hmm, %CrimeGoldTurnIn septims, I can make sure the guards know this was all just a mistake.
Such a shame. You should reconsider. Just think of all the widows you'd be helping to lift out of poverty. Their starving children. Homeless veterans of the Arnesian war.

Good choice. Thank you. I'm sure the widows will be most grateful as well. I'll see to it that this is put to good use. In the meantime, I'll have a chat with the governor and see if I can't get your name cleared.
That's all you have? I think someone who was truly reformed would offer to donate a little more than that, %PCName. Perhaps you should do a little fundraising.
You want to deal with it yourself? Heh. Now I feel sorry for the law.
You can count on me, %PCRank. I'll fight the law, and the law won't win. Consider yourself in the clear.
Ah, %PCRank, I don't think this is enough to cover the necessary bribes. I'll need %CrimeGoldDiscount drakes to clear everything up.

The Empire's the best thing that ever happened to this province, let me tell you. Left to its own devices, this place would descend into chaos in no time. You just have to look at the Ashlands and Telvanni country to see that. Murderers everywhere. The common man, crushed under a wizard's pointy bug boot. If you're stuck in Vvardenfell, stay here in Hlaalu territory. They're at least mostly civilized.
Larrius Varro is one of the Legion officers here at Fort Moonmoth. You can normally find him downstairs, twiddling his thumbs and chatting to every flea-bitten peddler that passes through.

All these adventurers are so quick to resort to their swords - must be something about this place, the natives positively encourage it. That's fine if you're a heroic knight or what have you, but it gets we lesser mortals killed more often than not. Try to resolve things peacefully if you can. If that means swallowing your pride or lining a few pockets along the way, so be it. It's so depressing seeing case after case of fools getting themselves killed squabbling over trinkets or drunken insults.

The Dark Elves resent Imperial influence because they want to cling to their backward customs instead of catching up with the rest of us, and some of them are angry enough about it to plot treason. What they don't realise is the Empire has eyes and ears everywhere. All the fools are doing is stealing enough rope to hand to the gallowman when the time comes. Sad, isn't it?
House Hlaalu is offering a reward for anyone who comes forward with information about some supposed long lost ebony mine. A wild goblin chase, if you ask me. Who loses an ebony mine?

Some Khajiit was in here a while back, crying about her lost Dark Elf friend. Omren-something, I think it was. Couldn't help her, of course, I'd never heard tell of the poor devil. Thought it was odd, though. Not often you hear of Dark Elves making nice with the beast races.

A Khajiit woman came in here a while back, crying about her lost Dark Elf friend. Omren or something. Couldn't help her, sadly, I'd never heard tell of the poor devil. Thought it was odd, though. Not often you hear of Dark Elves making nice with Khajiit. I've got nothing against your lot myself, of course, but then Cyrodiil's a bit more civilised than this place, isn't it?

You've heard about the murders, then? A whole group of local business owners, slaughtered in their club, and the Legion does nothing. Larrius Varo tells me he's on the hunt for the murderers, but where are the arrests? Terrible business. Just terrible.

They're a group of local businesspeople. They know how the world works, and that makes them a pleasure to deal with. Mostly. Shame about all the problems they've been having with the Thieves' Guild. But that's this province for you, I suppose.
Nolus Atrius is often called away on official business. I am his deputy here in Balmora. How may I help?
The bad magistrate is dead, and suddenly the criminals the good officer catches are staying in jail. Isn't it funny how life works like that sometimes?
Just like the bad magistrate in my little story, he's an important man, with important friends. And no shortage of drakes.
Nolus Atrius is our local magistrate. He makes himself scarce around here. If you have business with the magistrate's office, his deputy is Carolus Allectus. He's usually in his room upstairs.

Nolus Atrius is the Imperial magistrate for Balmora district. If you need to speak to him... Good luck. He's very rarely here. His deputy, Carolus Allectus, should be around here somewhere though. He normally keeps to his rooms near the shrine when he's not in court.
Whose family tomb? Some Dark Elf? What would you want to go poking around in there for? I'd be careful, if I were you. They don't much appreciate grave-robbing around here.
Yes? Is this about an official matter? Ah. I see. You're %PCName, and you have a price on your head. Come in, take a seat and tell me all about it.
Hello again, %PCName. Is this an official matter, or are you here for something else?
Oh, hello. Is this about an official matter? Do you have a price on your head? If you need the Imperial Cult, you've got the wrong room. The god-fearing sorts are all next door.
Nerevarine? Is that some local thing? I've never heard of it.

They're a guild of assassins. Unlike the Dark Brotherhood, their operations are perfectly legal. They have special protection under the terms of the Armistice, much the same way slavers do. I wouldn't cross them if I could help it, %PCName, the Empire can't do much to help you if they've got a writ out on you.

As you might imagine, I'm from Cyrodiil originally. My family have estates north of Leyawiin - Count Caro is a good friend of my mother's. I did a turn as a knight in the Count's service, then retired to study law in the Imperial City. I would have preferred a posting there, of course, but the Empire had need of talent out here in the provinces, so here I am, eh?
Something to do with the local religion, I think. You'd be better off asking an elf.

It's an island somewhere off the north coast of Vvardenfell. An icy wasteland, from what I've heard, but word is they've struck ebony. The East Empire Company is recruiting miners and shipping them out to build a colony, so there must be some truth to that. I'd go enquire at Fort Frostmoth if you're interested.

I am the deputy magistrate for the West Gash region of Vvardenfell District, appointed by Nolus Atrius. I primarily handle minor cases here - theft, criminal damage, assaults, public disorder, commercial disputes and the like. Anything particularly juicy, treason and what have you, has to be sent to Ebonheart, but we do get the occasional murder that has to be dealt with. And if you have any information on the Thieves Guild scum that keeps causing trouble in the city, I would love to hear all about it.

It's due just East of here, a warm, rocky dip in the landscape filled with Strider husks. We do what we can to comfort the passing Striders attracted there by the heat, and in return feel we've earned the right to harvest our chitin from their carcasses.
If you're planning on heading into the wastes, stay clear of the Strider Burial. Word is there's a particularly territorial Mabrigash that's moved in.
I hear you've taken care of that Mabrigash at the Strider Burial, we Urshilaku are in your debt.

What? You say these are not Daedric weapons? No, you are right, but Ra'Virr is no liar. When you wish it, Ra'Virr's Fiend, Demon, and Devil weapons will be as sharp as fine Daedric and as light as a netch air sac, if you have enough skill in Conjuration. The magic lasts a short time, but long enough to punch through the toughest armor. Ra'Virr buys them direct from the Telvanni. You'll not find any cheaper in all Balmora.
